chunks: What we mentioned was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Qāsim ibn Burayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The ghusl of the deceased is like the ghusl of janābah, and if he has abundant hair, then pour extra water over him three times. And that which opposes it...

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water used for the ritual washing
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ: three times; the stated number for additional pouring
key_terms.غُسْلُ: ritual washing; here, the prescribed washing of the deceased
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath performed for the state of janābah, used here as the model

ai.seo_question: How is the ghusl of a deceased person performed in relation to the ghusl of janābah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the ghusl of the deceased, stating that it is performed like the ghusl of janābah. It also instructs that if the deceased has abundant hair, additional water should be poured over him three times.
